title: What Must Be Ours
passage:
When Yui's class planned a school festival, everyone wanted the classroom to look exciting. Some students suggested buying many decorations. Others wanted to build everything by hand. The class had only a small budget, so they needed a plan that would make the room attractive without spending too much money. Yui suggested borrowing materials from other classes and using things that were already available at school. At first, some classmates thought borrowed decorations would make their room look less original. Yui asked them to list what they truly needed to create themselves and what could be shared. The class decided that the main sign and game materials should be original because those things represented their idea. However, tables, lights, cloth, and storage boxes did not need to be unique. They borrowed some items from the art club and others from a class that was holding its event on a different floor. This created a new problem. The students had to keep track of who owned each item. Yui made small labels and a simple checklist. Each borrowed object had a number, the owner's name, and the place where it should be returned. The system seemed unnecessary at first, but it became useful when the festival ended and everyone was tired. After cleaning the room, the class returned every borrowed item. They had spent less than half of their original budget and still had enough money to replace a broken game part during the festival. Their teacher asked what they had learned. One student said the best idea was not a decoration itself but the decision to separate what must be ours from what only needs to work. Yui agreed. A week later, another class asked to borrow the labels and checklist for a sports event. Yui was pleased because even the management system could be shared. She realized that originality does not mean creating every object from zero. Sometimes a project becomes stronger when people save their effort for the parts that carry the main idea and share ordinary tools for the rest. The classroom looked colorful, but the most useful lesson was about choosing carefully where to put time, money, and energy.

The class also wrote a short guide for the next year's students. It listed which items could be borrowed, how to label them, and when to return them. By passing on the method, they saved future students from solving the same small management problems again from the beginning.
translation:
結衣のクラスが文化祭を計画したとき、みんな教室を楽しく見せたいと考えました。飾りをたくさん買う案も、すべて手作りする案も出ましたが、予算は限られていました。そこで結衣は、他のクラスから借りたり、学校にすでにある物を使ったりすることを提案します。『借り物では独自性がなくなる』という声に対し、結衣は『自分たちで作る必要がある物』と『共有してもよい物』を分けて考えるよう促しました。メインの看板やゲーム道具は自分たちの考えを表すのでオリジナルにし、机、照明、布、収納箱などは借りることにしました。すると次に、誰の物か分からなくなる問題が出ます。結衣は番号、持ち主、返却場所を書いた小さなラベルとチェックリストを作りました。最初は面倒に見えた仕組みでしたが、文化祭終了後、疲れている中で片づけるときに大いに役立ち、すべて正しく返却できました。費用も当初予算の半分以下に抑えられ、途中で壊れたゲーム部品を買い直す余裕も残りました。先生に学んだことを聞かれた生徒は、『自分たちの物である必要がある部分と、機能すればよい部分を分けたこと』が最も大切だったと答えました。後日、別のクラスがスポーツ行事のためにそのラベルとチェックリストを借りに来ました。結衣は、管理の仕組みまで共有できることに気づきます。独自性とは何もかもゼロから作ることではなく、中心となる部分に力を集中し、普通の道具は共有することで、よりよい活動にできるのだと学びました。

クラスは翌年の生徒向けに、借りられる物、ラベルの付け方、返却時期をまとめた短い案内も残しました。方法を引き継ぐことで、次の生徒が同じ小さな管理問題を最初から解き直す必要を減らすことができました。
